On SEC-bench Pro, which evaluates long-horizon vulnerability discovery and proof-of-concept generation across complex software targets, GPT‑5.5‑Cyber reached 69.8%, compared with 63.1% for GPT‑5.5.

Our instantiation binds adapters for the Chromium Issue … Tracker [13] and Mozilla Bugzilla [32], restricting ingestion to … sec-high or sec-critical reports for SpiderMonkey and to … bounty-qualified or fix-landed bugs for V8 [12].
Reports that … lack either a concrete PoC or a linked fix are deferred because … the subsequent validation stage requires both to compute the … two-sided oracle.
For the Linux kernel, stage one takes … CVE-backed reports from kernelCTF [15] and syzbot [16] that … ship a triggering reproducer and a linked upstream fix commit.

Manual reconstruction at the scale of hundreds of bugs is infeasible, so SEC-bench Pro delegates the task to autonomous coding agents running inside sandboxed Docker harnesses that expose shell, file, and build tools.
The prompt forbids fabricated outputs and requires the agent to save the real captured stderr, which prevents the benchmark from accepting hallucinated reproductions.

This pipeline yields 344 instances across three targets in … two execution families: 103 V8 instances from the Chromium … issue tracker [13], 104 SpiderMonkey instances from Mozilla Bugzilla [32] and related advisory sources [8, 29, 58], and 137 CVE-backed Linux kernel … instances from kernelCTF [15] and syzbot [16].
The V8 subset spans 86 bounty-qualified … reports with a cumulative VRP award of $1,540,750 and the … Linux subset combines 89 kernelCTF and 48 syzbot instances.

We present SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark for agentic bug hunting built from 344 reproducible instances across V8, SpiderMonkey, and the Linux kernel, together with three-image grading that recovers valid PoCs discarded by simpler graders.
Our runs also surfaced three vulnerabilities and earned a $20,000 Google VRP bounty.

The prompt fixes a three-level taxonomy for each … PoC run: E1 a vulnerability crash (sanitizer and KASAN reports, … sandbox violations, DCHECK failures, and runtime crashes), … E2 a harmless outcome (clean exits, ordinary language-level … exceptions, and mitigation messages), and E3 an infrastructure … failure (resource exhaustion, missing files, unrecognized flags, … and timeouts).

Linux evaluations additionally require an x86-64 Linux host whose Docker daemon can expose a readable and writable /dev/kvm to a privileged container. This includes enabling nested virtualization when evaluating from a cloud VM. The benchmark does not support QEMU TCG as an equivalent grading mode: it changes execution time and scheduling, and can invalidate time-sensitive PoCs.
